messages:
jane_cust: Hey team — our private deployment (us-west-2, customer-vpc) keeps dropping streaming responses around ~9 minutes. Client sees "stream closed" and partial output. Not seeing errors on our app side.

jamie_support: Sorry you're hitting this. Quick q: is this via our Private package behind a customer-managed firewall/proxy?

jane_cust: yes, traffic goes through corporate NGFW (Palo Alto) and an internal NAT appliance before hitting our infra. We only see the initial request reach Redwood, then the stream gets cut.

alex_sre: Can you share the exact symptoms + a short repro? e.g., curl or simple Python streaming request that fails reproducibly.

jane_cust: Repro steps: 1) start a streaming call to /v1/streams with model=gpt-4-lite-prod 2) wait ~8-10 minutes while tokens stream 3) connection closes with no further frames. curl log attached (trimmed):

```
$ curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer ***" https://private.redwood.example.com/v1/streams/abc -N
* Connected to private.redwood.example.com (3.120.45.10) port 443 (#0)
> GET /v1/streams/abc HTTP/1.1
> Host: private.redwood.example.com
> ...
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
< content-type: text/event-stream
data: {"delta":"..."}
[... streaming tokens for ~9 minutes ...]
* Received HTTP/2 stream reset
* Closing connection 0

```

jamie_support: Thanks. Can you grab a tcpdump on the client side and a packet capture on the NAT (if possible) around the disconnect time? We want to see if packets stop or a RST is injected.

jane_cust: tcpdump from client shows nothing for ~600s, then an RST from the firewall to our client at timestamp 00:09:59. pcap snippet:

```
09:00:00.123 IP client -> redwood 443: TLS application data
... (steady small bursts)
09:09:59.999 IP firewall -> client 443: RST, seq 0
```

alex_sre: Interesting — firewall RST at ~600s. Many NGFWs default to a 600s TCP flow idle timeout and treat TLS streams with infrequent small records as idle. Are you using application-level heartbeats only (some SDKs send keepalive events inside the TLS stream) vs. OS-level TCP keepalives?

raj_network: Also check NAT session timeout on the NAT appliance. If NAT mapping expires at ~600s, the firewall/NAT may consider the flow dead and tear it down.

jane_cust: Our app sends a ping event every 30s inside the event stream, but that's inside TLS and sometimes gets coalesced. The firewall may not see small inside-TLS activity. We don't currently have OS TCP keepalives enabled.

jamie_support: Two quick checks: 1) run a continuous small-packet test that sends a tiny TCP probe (openssl s_client or h2load with small frames) to see if the firewall still drops. 2) On a test host, enable TCP keepalive and set keepalive_time < firewall timeout and retest. Example commands:

```
# enable TCP keepalive in Linux for current session
sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_keepalive_time=60
sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_keepalive_intvl=10
sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_keepalive_probes=5

# tcpdump to watch for keepalive probes (uses small payloads)
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 host 3.120.45.10 and tcp

# simple TLS connection test
openssl s_client -connect private.redwood.example.com:443 -quiet -tls1_2
# then type something small / wait >10m
```

alex_sre: If enabling TCP keepalive prevents the drop, that's strong evidence the firewall is using an idle timeout and not seeing the kept-alive activity inside the TLS stream. Long-term fixes: request the NGFW team to increase the TCP idle timeout for that destination prefix or allow long-lived streams, or keep OS-level keepalives enabled on clients and any proxy/NAT in path.

raj_network: Another potential fix is to pin source port preservation on the NAT (if supported) so intermediate devices consistently see activity on the same tuple — some appliances aggressively tear NAT mappings when ports rotate. But try keepalives first.

jane_cust: We'll try the sysctl change and run a lengthy repro. If that works, ops will open a ticket with the firewall team to adjust idle timeout. Any recommendations for timeout value?

jamie_support: Recommend >1h if you expect very long streams. We commonly ask for 3600s (1 hour) or disable short timeouts for that flow. Also recommend whitelist the Redwood endpoint IPs on the firewall to avoid DPI/timeouts for streaming content.

alex_sre: FYI if you can share a pcap showing the RST and your tcp_keepalive-enabled pcap showing no RST, we can close the loop on our side and document in the private deployment runbook.

jane_cust: Understood — I'll attach pcaps shortly. Thanks for the quick triage. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: New file uploaded: repro_pcap_3790000123.pcap (private link)

jamie_support: great — when you have the pcap we'll validate and propose wording for the firewall change request to share with your network/security team.

jane_cust: Uploaded keepalive-enabled test pcap too. Initial look: keepalive prevents RST. We'll coordinate firewall change and confirm.

jamie_support: Perfect. I'll mark this thread as tracked. If anything changes or you see different error (e.g., TLS handshake failures vs RST), ping here and include the openssl debug output.

jane_cust: Will do. Thanks everyone!
